There are a lot of points I disagree with you on, and this is coming from a guy who uses an AR15 for home defense over a shotgun.

  • "Spread is much less than people think. (pattern a PDF shotgun at the range if you don't believe me)"

That's not a limitation of shotguns as much as it is not the advantage some people think it is specifically at home-defense distances.

  • "00 Buck (best pdf load) is defeated by even soft armor"

It certainly wont pierce body armor, but if the person being shot with 00 buckshot is wearing soft body armor it can still potentially be lethal and will require an emergency trip to the hospital.

  • "Extreme load times"

That almost certainly wont matter in a home defense situation. Yes, home invasions now, on average, involve more people, but they almost always run away once the home owner starts shooting regardless of what they're being shot at with.

  • "You basically pay the same time penalty between each shot as if you had to clear a jam on an AR"

That's really biased. Clearing a jam on an AR15 takes much longer than racking the pump on a pump action shotgun. What you could put as a legitimate limitation of pump shotguns in particular is the ability of the user to short-shuck the pump. The chances of a used-induced malfunction with a pump is much larger than the chance of a decently mainted AR15 jamming.

  • "Heat issues with sustained fire."

No one is going to be firing a shotgun in a legitimate self defense situation enough times for the barrel heating to be a serious concern.

  • "Shorter operating radius (assuming your shotgun has a stock)"

A 20" barrel ar15 with a fixed stock (or adjustable stock fully extended) is about as long as a shotgun with a fixed stock an an 18.5" barrel. AR15s can be and usually are shorter.

  • "Ability to deliver sustained fire while moving"

You can do the same with a shotgun.

Here is what I'd suggest is a more accurate pros and cons of a pump shotgun vs ar15 for home defense

Pump shotgun pros

1: Inexpensive.

A decent pump shotgun can be had for about $200. Even in the golden-age of AR15s, an AR15 would usually cost at minimum about $350 (and right now those days seem so far gone). The pump shotgun doesn't (almost) require additional magazines like the AR15, it does ship from the factory with sights (unlike some "optics-read" ar15s), etc. Just $200 and it's good to go. Hopefully a light gets added, sure, but that would cost about the same whether it's added to an ar15 or a pump shotgun regardless.

2: Incredibly lethal.

AR15s in 5.56 or whatever are plenty lethal, don't get me wrong, but just as rifles are on a completely different, higher level of lethality over a pistol, shotguns vs. unarmored targets at close disances are on their own, even higher level of lethality over your typical rifle. If you want the person being shot to be dead immediately, as in the body already being a corpse before it hits the floor, then one's best bet is a shotgun.

Pump shotgun cons

1: High-recoil

This can be mitigated somewhat with good ammo selection, but in general shotguns have pretty severe recoil. This makes practice uncomfortable and therefore most-often an uncommon occurrence, especially for women and children.

2: Prone to user-induced malfunction (short shucking)

Pump shotguns are easy to accidentally short-shuck, especially without practice and while under stress (as most people would be if they had to defend themselves). I think the likelihood of short-shucking a shotgun is much higher than a well made and maintained auto-loading firearm jamming.

I wouldn't put low ammunition capacity or long reload times as a con as I don't see those as serious concerns for a home-defense firearm, at least not when each shot you do get off is as lethal as a shotgun.

AR15 Pros

1: Low-recoil

At least when shooting 5.56 NATO, the AR15 is about as low-recoil as a serious use long-gun can be. This makes for faster follow up shots and the ability for anyone to use the firearm effectively.

2: Larger magazine capacity and faster reloads

Although I wouldn't list the lack of these two things as a con for the shotgun (considering realisitic home defense situations and how lethal a shotgun is), that doesn't stop me as listing it as a pro for the AR15.

3: Longer-range

Some people aren't just defending a suburban home from the inside; some people defend their land and livestock from a distance. The longer range of an AR15 helps dramatically in these specific situations.

4: Defeats armor more easily

The AR15, specifically in 5.56 NATO, is able to defeat the most commonly used forms of body armor.

5: Better suited to defense from tyranny

This is really more of a combination of a few points, but between the higher capacity, faster reloads, ability to defeat armor, and longer effective range, if one is defending themselves not from common burglars but from tyrants then the AR15 is much better suited to the job.

AR15 cons

1: Takes slightly more knowledge to operate effectively.

The AR15 is not rocket science, but you'd be surprised how many people aren't willing or able to understand how to operate an AR15. People who don't care and have it explained to them how to operate something like an AR15 are very likely to forget what they were told. This would encompass a lot of wives. As long as someone genuinely wants to know how an AR15 works then this almost always isn't an issue.

Shotguns present a number of substantial drawbacks in home defense application.

  1. Capacity- obviously shotguns have dramatically reduced capacity compared to pistols or carbines. Anyone who makes the claim that "you don't need all those extra rounds" or "if ya can't put'em down with 6 shots, you should just lay down and die" has never had any sort of defensive firearms training and is not someone who should ever be taken seriously when discussing defensive firearms application. You can not predict how many threats will be involved, what type of threat they will be, or how many shots it will take to remove the threat.
  2. Manual of Arms- contrary to absurdly misinformed belief, shotguns, particularly pump action shotguns, are dramatically more difficult to manipulate effectively under stress. They require both hands to be on the gun at all times to function, and in untrained, injured, or weak hands can be rendered entirely ineffective by a short stroked rack, not to mention the ridiculous single shell reloading requirements. It takes a substantial amount of training to become sufficiently proficient with a shotgun to be effective as a defensive weapon.
  3. Recoil- defensive shotgun loads universally have a higher recoil than comparable 5.56mm defensive loads, resulting in reduced followup speed and accuracy under stress.
  4. Overpenetration- this is a relatively minor but inexplicably overemphasized issue, regardless of platform. All effective defensive ammunition, irrespective of caliber or weapon type, WILL PENETRATE RESIDENTIAL BARRIER MATERIALS. It is entirely unavoidable, and in reality should be considered a relative nonissue when choosing a defensive firearm or load. That being said, the CATEGORICAL majority of decades of empirical ballistic testing has proven that 5.56mm defensive loads (and even trash plinking ammo like 55grain m193 ball) penetrates with LESS mass and energy retention than comparable 12 gauge and pistol caliber defensive loads, resulting in a REDUCED(ie, NOT eliminated) risk of collateral injury. Some will speak of using birdshot in order to minimize overpenetration risk, but birdshot has been consistently proven to exhibit abhorrent terminal ballistics, easily defeated by heavy clothing, and with insufficient soft tissue penetration to reach vital organs or nerve systems for reliable medical stops. Anyone who defends the use of birdshot as a viable defensive load is horribly misinformed.

It is important to understand that none of these drawbacks make shotguns useless as defensive weapons. Shotguns still exhibit devastating damage on threat targets when used properly and effectively. However, if one is looking objectively, without emotional investment or bias, for the ideal home defense weapon with currently available technology and training protocols, shotguns have simply been outclassed by intermediate caliber carbines and carbine pattern pistols.
